focus: Extractor fields, unchecked edge operators and dead markup checks
noveltyJustification: Four findings are genuinely new (unchecked edge operators, two dead markup marks, cleaning behavior, extractor caps) and eight are partial or restatements; (4 + 0.5*8) / 12 = 0.667, reported as 0.70 with the edge-gap weight.
keyQuestions: Which layout, colour, shape, density and label limits does the corpus treat as enforceable versus advisory, and do they support or contradict Flow Mode's limits (TD only, 9 nodes, 3 decision exits, one accent colour, four shapes)?
ruledOut: Adding a parser change for edge rules
Treating a reserved word in a label as a defect

label: Every proposed check has its data already: Node exposes id, label and shape, and Edge exposes style, arrowhead, bidirectional and undirected.
New gap: flow_check.py never validates edge operators, so undirected, bidirectional, dashed and thick edges all pass.
The edge rule should require a solid, one-directional connector with the arrow at the target, since undirected and bidirectional connectors contradict a directed flow.
Two of the five markup marks are dead: clean_label strips tags and emphasis before the checker sees a label, so <, > and ** can never match.
Only the line-break mark survives cleaning, so the rule rejects line breaks but not markup, narrower than its docstring claims.
The raw Mermaid text still carries markup to the generator, so a markup model passes the check and is silently cleaned rather than rejected.
Backticks are stripped only when they wrap the whole label, so the backtick mark is dead for the common case.
Emoji survives cleaning, so the emoji rule runs on node.label and edge.label without a raw-text scan.
Node IDs are never cleaned, so reserved-word and underscore rules test node.id exactly as written.
The extractor's 2000-node and 5000-edge caps do not shadow Flow Mode's nine-node rule, so the ten-node planted test is reachable.
The subgraph scan must be anchored to a statement start so a label containing the word does not false-positive.
The edge rule and the board read-back can share one vocabulary, mapping model style and arrowhead onto strokeDashes and cap fields.
